description: I’m a university student in Riyadh interested in health technology, space science, and digital innovation. I enjoy designing websites and building interactive prototypes. Our team, NEXUS BOTH, aims to explore solutions for astronaut health. We welcome members interested in programming, data analysis, medical research, and teamwork.
summary:
ASTRA DECISION LAB is a research prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring and Extravehicular Activity (EVA) mission planning.

The platform brings together NASA research datasets, separately recorded daily health measurements, and clearly identified simulated EVA scenarios in an interactive decision-support environment.

Users can explore astronaut health indicators, record and track daily measurements, compare current values with personal baselines, and review changes over time. The platform also enables mission teams to explore hypothetical EVA scenarios and compare potential operational adjustments.

By combining health monitoring, time-based analysis, and scenario simulation, ASTRA supports a structured workflow: Monitor, Analyze, Evaluate, Adapt, Simulate, and Reassess.

ASTRA is a research prototype, not a diagnostic tool or an autonomous medical decision system.
details:
ASTRA DECISION LAB is an interactive research prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring and EVA mission decision-making.

The platform brings together health observations, sleep and recovery indicators, and mission requirements to help users explore how crew well-being may influence mission planning.

The system includes six main modules:

• Overview: Provides a centralized view of the platform and its purpose.

• Crew Health: Explores astronaut-related health indicators using NASA research data.

• Sleep Recovery: Examines sleep duration, efficiency, and recovery patterns.

• Mission Setup: Allows users to configure mission conditions.

• Scenario Lab: Compares alternative mission and recovery strategies.

• Decision Report: Presents scenario findings and decision-support insights.

The platform follows a Monitor, Analyze, Evaluate, Adapt, Simulate, and Reassess workflow.

Technology used:

• Python

• Streamlit

• Pandas

• Plotly

• NASA Open Science Data Repository datasets

ASTRA uses research datasets and clearly identified simulated scenarios. The datasets represent different studies and cohorts and are not treated as continuous measurements from the same astronauts.

The expected benefit is to help mission planners explore health-related considerations and operational trade-offs before EVA activities. ASTRA is a decision-support research prototype, not a certified medical system. It does not diagnose medical conditions or autonomously approve missions. Final decisions require qualified human review.
